explained.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials at White House

happened.text: US First Lady Melania Trump hosted senior Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House to call for a more enduring ceasefire following a recent truce in Kherson.
US President Donald Trump held an unscheduled meeting with Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev and predicted a major agreement involving Europe.
Delegations from both sides praised Melania Trump for helping to broker the six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky.

background.text: The conflict began when Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The delegations visiting Washington included Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, Ukrainian Member of Parliament Davyd Arakhamia, and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev.

matters.text: Ukrainian MP Davyd Arakhamia stated that the Oleshky ceasefire constituted the biggest de-escalation since 2022 and helped both sides learn the mechanics of keeping the peace.
The Guardian reported that Donald Trump's comments will fuel European concerns that he is pivoting towards the Kremlin and pressing Ukraine towards an unfavourable deal.

uncertain.text: Donald Trump refused to disclose what he discussed with the Kremlin envoy, and the exact nature of Melania Trump's involvement in coordinating the ceasefire remains unelaborated by Moscow and Kyiv.
Local government sources in Kherson noted that evacuation work had been ongoing for nearly a year, making it difficult to determine who played what role at each stage.

problems: The text mentions a recent truce in Kherson, but does not explain how this relates to Oleshky.
The phrase an unfavourable deal is used without prior introduction or context regarding what the deal entails.

explained.headline: European airlines and airports targeted in second wave of hoax bomb threats

happened.text: At least 21 aircraft and several airports across Europe were targeted by bomb threats in the second such incident within a week.

background.text: The latest warnings were signed on behalf of a group or individual calling themselves Fighters of the Male State, which likely refers to a banned Russian ultra-right organisation.
A similar wave of security alerts occurred earlier in the week, involving flights searched after mid-air or pre-flight threats.

uncertain.text: Authorities stated it remains unclear whether the various threats are connected or if copycats are simply reproducing the disruptions.

terms.definition: The corporate body responsible for managing the airport system in Italy's capital city.

removed.text: Fighter jets escorted multiple flights, including Finnair and Ryanair services, while other planes were diverted or met by police upon landing.

removed.text: Searches by police and military personnel yielded no explosives, and UK officials described the warnings as malicious hoaxes.
why: Evidence does not mention military personnel searches, and the claim misses required attribution for the hoax assessment.

removed.text: Experts warned that a high volume of false alarms risks breeding complacency among aviation authorities or serving as a deliberate diversion.
why: The claim omits the expert's hedge that these are potential, not definitive, risks.

removed.text: Analysts suggested the incidents form part of a pattern of cheap and deniable disruption directed at commercial air travel.
why: The claim omits attribution to experts and removes the hedge that this is a possible pattern.

removed.text: Experts noted that the short duration of the incidents provides too small a sample to determine whether the warnings are coordinated or contagious.
why: The claim presents expert opinion as objective fact without proper attribution.
